findings.evidence: AEMO 2026 states WRL is anticipated and expected to be completed in November 2029, which falls in the chart year 2029. The 2024 representation said mid-2027; see CONTRADICTION warning.

No archived source states a WRL cost of $1.6 billion, or any standalone WRL estimate. The only archived WRL-specific amount is $315 million in 2020-21 (FY2020-21) dollars, stated by AEMO 2024 as included within the VNI West quoted project cost of $3,499 million - a different boundary, price basis and date. The now-archived joint VNI West PACR (VNV-TRANSGRID-2023-PACR, the primary source AEMO's 2024 summary draws on) independently states the same $315 million WRL incremental cost, itemised separately as 'Included cost' within both the Option 5 ($3,406m) and Option 5A ($3,499m) all-states totals, and describes it as the direct cost of modifying WRL so it can connect VNI West at Bulgana. supported_value is in AUD million, not the chart's AUD billion; no conversion is asserted. Both AEMO project tables leave WRL's reported/expected cost blank. See SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warnings for the 2019 PACR, VicGrid/NEVA and the AusNet cost update, and the AUTHOR_DECISION_REQUIRED note on the chart's $1.6 billion figure's likely origin.

AusNet states WRL is 'Capable of carrying more than 3,000MW of energy' - a proponent capability lower bound on an undefined basis, matching the chart's 3 GW in magnitude only. AEMO's project-specific figures are different quantities: 1,460 MW renewable capacity harnessed, 695 MW additional MEL-WNV network capacity and V2 310 MW. supported_value is in MW. The 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order (VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267) states only qualitative benefits for WRL ('alleviating network constraints and increasing hosting capacity in Victoria's west') and states no WRL capacity figure of any kind.
findings.pages: WRL-AUSNET-PROJECT derivative line 49; HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 pp24-25; VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267 p11

findings.evidence: AusNet describes WRL as a proposed new 190 kilometre overhead line from Bulgana to Sydenham, the same trunk the chart measures. Neither AEMO ISP appendix states a route length.

Chart calculation: $1.6 billion divided by 190 km. The length input is supported (WRL-AO-2026-TRUNK-190KM) but the cost input is not: no archived source states $1.6 billion for WRL, so this ratio inherits an unsupported numerator. See CHART_DERIVATION warning.

AEMO 2026 describes a planned 500 kV double-circuit overhead line from Bulgana to Sydenham, and the delivery scope specifies switched shunt line reactors at the end of each circuit. The 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order's Schedule 2 (VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267), the legal instrument specifying the WRL Uprate, independently corroborates this: a new 500 kV double-circuit SYTS-BGTS line with switched shunt line reactors at the end of each circuit.

AEMO 2026 delivery scope states a single new transmission line: 'A new 500 kV double-circuit transmission line from Sydenham Terminal Station to Bulgana Terminal Station'. The 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order's Schedule 2 (VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267) independently specifies the same single new line, SYTS to BGTS, as the WRL Uprate augmentation.
Author definition. No archived source counts alternative routes for WRL. The 2019 RIT-T option set and the WRL EES route alternatives are unarchived, so a zero cannot be evidenced either way.

No archived source states a synchronous condenser rating for WRL, and none states that WRL includes no synchronous condensers. The AEMO 2026 delivery scope enumerates reactive plant as shunt line reactors (approximately 70 MVAr per circuit) and a 100 MVAr 500 kV switched bus reactor at Sydenham only; absence from an enumerated list is not a sourced zero. See AUTHOR_DECISION_REQUIRED.

Author definition. No archived source counts hubs. The 2026 delivery scope names works at Bulgana Terminal Station (new 500 kV switchyard), Sydenham Terminal Station (extension, bays, bus reactor) and Elaine Terminal Station (cut-ins and realignment), plus minor augmentations at unnamed existing terminals, so a hub count of 1 reflects an author boundary choice. Bulgana is a shared WRL / VNI West terminal; see SHARED_ATTRIBUTION. The 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order's Schedule 2 (VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267) names a fourth WRL terminal not enumerated in AEMO's 2024/2026 delivery scope summaries: Ballarat Terminal Station (BATS), where new 220 kV circuit breakers establish double switching on the existing bays. A hub count of 1 therefore also excludes a fourth, order-specified terminal.

Chart calculation: the sum of two 1,000 MVA units. AEMO 2026 states a new 500 kV switchyard at Bulgana Terminal Station with two new 500/220 kV 1,000 MVA transformers (WRL-AO-2026-TRANSFORMERS-1000; 2024 equivalent WRL-AO-2024-TRANSFORMERS-1000). The per-unit rating is preserved rather than summed in observations. These transformers sit at the shared Bulgana terminal; see SHARED_ATTRIBUTION. The 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order's Schedule 2 (VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267), the legal instrument specifying the WRL Uprate, independently states the same two 500/220 kV 1,000 MVA transformers at the new Bulgana switchyard (WRL-AO-2023-TRANSFORMERS-1000).

summary.analysis_conclusion: No WRL cost of any date or boundary is archived beyond a $315 million WRL amount stated as included inside VNI West's $3,499 million 2020-21-dollar quoted cost. The chart's $1.6 billion and the derived $/km therefore have no source, and the transformer and hub cells rest on shared Bulgana plant that cannot be allocated. Capacity, length, circuits, lines and the 2029 date are sourced, on differing definitions.
summary.capacity: AEMO: 1,460 MW of renewable capacity harnessed under the uprated scope (600 MW original design), 695 MW additional MEL-WNV network capacity and 310 MW REZ V2. AusNet separately claims capability of more than 3,000 MW.
summary.current_status: Anticipated project in the AEMO 2026 ISP; EES public hearing concluded 3 March 2026 with no archived outcome. Not committed, approved or funded on the archived record.
summary.delivery_status: Anticipated (AEMO 2026 classification); construction status not evidenced.
summary.dependent_projects: VNI West (connects at a terminal station near Bulgana; WRL is an interface/prerequisite). South West Victoria Expansion is a separate future project with a WRL prerequisite. Western Victoria Reinforcement is a distinct VicGrid program, not a WRL component.
summary.funding_pathway: Not established in the archive. No RIT-T PACR, NEVA order, regulatory determination or funding instrument was acquired.
summary.identity: One continuous WRL Project, formerly named Western Victoria Transmission Network Project. The physical line, terminals, reactors, transformers and protection/control works are Components; the May 2023 uprate and North Ballarat terminal relocation is a scope Version. VNI West is a distinct related Project sharing the Bulgana terminal interface.
summary.name: Western Renewables Link
summary.owner: AusNet is the archived proponent; Victorian transmission planning responsibility transferred to VicGrid on 1 November 2025. No ownership or delivery instrument is archived.
summary.schedule: AEMO 2026 expects completion November 2029, superseding the 2024 mid-2027 / July-2027 representation. Not energisation or commercial operation.

timeline.detail: AEMO records that a RIT-T was completed in July 2019; the original design was 600 MW. The PACR itself was not acquired.

timeline.detail: Minor line augmentations on Red Cliffs-Wemen-Kerang-Bendigo and Moorabool-Terang-Ballarat 220 kV lines completed through AusNet Services NCIPAP.

North Ballarat terminal station relocated to Bulgana and the line from north of Ballarat to Bulgana uprated from 220 kV to 500 kV; capacity moves from 600 MW design to 1,460 MW. Underlying VNI West PACR remains unarchived; the NEVA order is now archived (VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267, Special Gazette S267, 27 May 2023) - see the 2023-05-27 timeline entry.

timeline.event: WRL PACR published by AEMO (precise date)

timeline.detail: Order dated 26 May 2023, published 27 May 2023. Schedule 2 specifies the WRL Uprate augmentation: a new 500 kV double-circuit line from Sydenham Terminal Station to Bulgana Terminal Station with two new 500/220 kV 1,000 MVA transformers at a new Bulgana switchyard, plus works at Sydenham, Ballarat and Elaine Terminal Stations. The reasons state the WRL segment from Mount Prospect ('north of Ballarat') to Bulgana was to be uprated from 220 kV to 500 kV and the Mount Prospect terminal site relocated to Bulgana, enabling additional generation capacity in Western Victoria 'by as early as 2027'. This order is the legal source underlying AEMO's later 2024/2026 ISP scope summaries.
timeline.event: VNI West and WRL Ministerial Order made under s16Y of the Electricity (Victoria) Act 2005, published as Special Gazette S267

timeline.detail: Recorded as Western Renewables Link (uprated), formerly named Western Victoria Transmission Network Project; anticipated, 1,460 MW, expected completion mid-2027 with July 2027 full capacity after testing.
Transmission network planning responsibilities transitioned from AEMO, through AEMO Victorian Planning, to VicGrid. This does not by itself establish WRL ownership.
timeline.event: Victorian transmission planning responsibility transferred to VicGrid

timeline.detail: AusNet states the WRL Environment Effects Statement public hearing concluded on 3 March 2026; no outcome or approval is stated and no EES record is archived.
Anticipated project, 500 kV double-circuit Bulgana to Sydenham, 1,460 MW harnessed, 695 MW additional MEL-WNV network capacity, V2 310 MW, expected completion November 2029, no reported cost.

AusNet announces appointment of a joint venture between ACCIONA and Genus to undertake WRL construction works, and describes the line as a proposed 190-kilometre 500 kV overhead line from near Bulgana to Sydenham. Construction can proceed if the project receives the necessary planning approvals; no cost figure is stated on the release.
timeline.event: AusNet appoints ACCIONA Genus Joint Venture as WRL construction contractor

timeline.detail: States a proposed 190 km Bulgana to Sydenham line and capability of more than 3,000 MW; gives no estimate and no completion date.

warnings.finding: The July 2019 AEMO Western Victoria Renewable Integration RIT-T PACR - the original decision, 600 MW design and original estimate basis - was not acquired after two distinct official routes returned HTTP 403.
warnings.implication: The 600 MW original design and the original cost basis rest on AEMO's later retrospective statements, not on the underlying decision record.
warnings.pinpoints: manifest row WRL-AEMO-2019-PACR (status unavailable); discovery WRL-AEMO-2019-PACR attempts 1-2

warnings.finding: The VicGrid WRL project record - the current Victorian planning authority's own project and NEVA-related material - was not acquired after two HTTP 403 attempts.
warnings.implication: Post-1-November-2025 ownership, planning status and any VicGrid cost or schedule statement are unverified; AusNet remains the only archived proponent record.
warnings.pinpoints: manifest row WRL-VICGRID-PROJECT (status unavailable); discovery WRL-VICGRID-PROJECT attempts 1-2

warnings.finding: No Environment Effects Statement, EES panel or Victorian approval record for WRL is archived; the only evidence of the EES process is the AusNet webpage line stating the public hearing concluded on 3 March 2026.
warnings.implication: Route alternatives, approval status and any EES-stated cost or schedule cannot be checked; the hearing outcome is unknown as at the 2026-09-03 cut-off.
warnings.pinpoints: WRL-AUSNET-PROJECT derivative line 75; no manifest row exists for an EES record

warnings.finding: The AusNet WRL design and construction cost update was not acquired: the design route returned HTTP 404 and the homepage returned HTTP 200 but carried no estimate.
warnings.implication: No proponent cost estimate of any date exists in the archive; the chart's $1.6 billion has no proponent source.
warnings.pinpoints: manifest row WRL-AUSNET-ESTIMATE (status unavailable); discovery WRL-AUSNET-ESTIMATE attempts 1-2

warnings.finding: Bulgana Terminal Station is a shared WRL / VNI West asset: AEMO 2026 states VNI West will connect at a terminal station near Bulgana to WRL, while the WRL delivery scope contains the new Bulgana 500 kV switchyard, the two 1,000 MVA 500/220 kV transformers and the second 220 kV bus.
warnings.implication: The transformer and hub cells rest on shared plant. No allocation between WRL and VNI West is made or inferable from the archive; do not attribute a share of Bulgana works, or their cost, to either project.
warnings.pinpoints: HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 p25 (WRL scope); p51 (VNI West connects at Bulgana)

warnings.finding: The $315m WRL amount, the $3,499m VNI West quoted cost and the $3,614m VNI West modelling cost are nested and overlapping: the $3,499m is inclusive of the $315m, and the $3,614m is the $3,499m with WRL removed and converted to 2023 dollars.
warnings.implication: Do not add WRL and VNI West amounts, and do not back-solve a WRL cost from the $3,614m modelling figure.

warnings.finding: The capacity figures in the archive measure different things: 600 MW original design, 1,460 MW renewable capacity harnessed, 695 MW additional MEL-WNV network capacity, 310 MW REZ V2, and AusNet's 'more than 3,000MW' carrying capability.
warnings.implication: Do not plot these as one capacity series or treat the chart's 3 GW as the same quantity as AEMO's 1,460 MW.
warnings.pinpoints: HUM-AEMO-2024-ISP-A5 p19; HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 pp24-25; WRL-AUSNET-PROJECT derivative line 49

warnings.finding: AEMO 2024 states expected completion mid-2027 (July 2027 for full capacity after testing); AEMO 2026 states November 2029. The 2024 and 2026 delivery scope tables also differ, the 2026 scope being materially longer. The 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order's reasons independently state the WRL Uprate would enable additional generation capacity in Western Victoria 'by as early as 2027', bounding the likely origin of the 2024 mid-2027 figure; the Order does not state a WRL completion date and does not mention 2029.
warnings.implication: Both versions are preserved. The chart's 2029 date reflects the current representation only; the earlier schedule is not silently overwritten.
warnings.pinpoints: HUM-AEMO-2024-ISP-A5 p19; HUM-AEMO-2026-ISP-A5 pp24-25; VNV-VIC-GAZETTE-2023-S267 p12

warnings.finding: Two chart cells are calculations: millions_per_trunk_km (1,600 / 190) and transformers 2000 MVA (2 x 1,000 MVA). The cost numerator of the first is not supported by any archived source.
warnings.implication: Publish millions_per_trunk_km only with the cost caveat attached; the transformer total is a sum of source-stated per-unit ratings at a shared terminal.

warnings.finding: On 1 November 2025 Victorian transmission planning responsibility transferred from AEMO Victorian Planning to VicGrid.
warnings.implication: Post-transfer WRL planning statements would come from VicGrid, whose record is unavailable; AEMO's 2026 representation may not reflect the current Victorian planning position.

warnings.finding: No WRL cost estimate, regulatory allowance, contract or outturn of any date is archived; both AEMO project tables leave the WRL cost column empty.
warnings.implication: The chart's cost and millions-per-km cells cannot be published as sourced figures as they stand.

warnings.finding: The cost cell is recorded as supported_with_boundary against the $315m WRL-within-VNI-West amount rather than as a gap.
warnings.implication: Author must confirm this framing, and confirm that supported_value 315 is read as AUD million on a 2020-21-dollar VNI West-internal basis and never rendered as the chart's $1.6 billion.

warnings.finding: The chart's $1.6 billion cost figure matches no archived WRL or VNI West amount of any date, price basis or boundary. Its magnitude appears to originate from an ASX filing or investor/market disclosure by the newly appointed construction contractor (AGJV, ACCIONA Genus Joint Venture) or a party to it, none of which is archived; the archived AusNet contractor-appointment release (WRL-AUSNET-2025-CONTRACTOR, 12 December 2025) confirms the 190 km route and names the contractor but states no cost figure.
warnings.implication: Author must identify and, if possible, acquire the ASX filing or other primary disclosure this figure may derive from before treating $1.6 billion as sourced; until then it remains unsupported, consistent with the OUTTURN_UNKNOWN blocker below.
warnings.pinpoints: WRL-AUSNET-2025-CONTRACTOR (no cost stated on the release); no ASX filing is archived or has a manifest row

warnings.finding: The network capacity cell is matched to AusNet's 'more than 3,000MW' capability rather than to AEMO's 1,460 MW harnessed capacity or 695 MW additional network capacity.
warnings.implication: Author must confirm which capacity definition the chart column means across all rows before publishing 3 GW for WRL.

warnings.finding: The hubs cell (1) and the syncons cell (0) are author positions: no source counts hubs, and no source states a synchronous condenser count or its absence.
warnings.implication: Author must fix a hub definition (Bulgana, Sydenham, Elaine and, per the 2023 s16Y Ministerial Order's Schedule 2, Ballarat Terminal Station all receive WRL terminal works, and Bulgana is shared with VNI West) and confirm whether an unenumerated syncon should read 0 or blank.

warnings.finding: The WRL EES public hearing concluded 3 March 2026 with no archived outcome, and VicGrid has held Victorian planning responsibility since 1 November 2025.
warnings.implication: Re-check the EES/panel outcome, any Victorian approval, and VicGrid's WRL record after the 2026-09-03 cut-off; a cost estimate is most likely to appear there.
